title: UniFi Network Application 11.1.58
summary:
Overview

UniFi Network Application 11.1.58 includes the improvements and bugfixes listed below.

Improvements

  • Added a Firmware Revert option for U5G devices.

  • Added support for local Firewall Policies when using Orchestration Engine Firewall Policies.

  • Added a Refresh Interval option to Historical Flows.

  • Added device progress indicators to Topology.

  • Added System Log events for public WAN IP address changes.

  • Added alarms for 5G SIM changes, client roaming, and AP channel changes.

  • Added Threat Signature filtering to Traffic Flows.

  • Added usage statistics to Object-Oriented Networking objects.

  • Added support for larger Live Flows counts.

    • Requires UniFi OS Gateway 6.1 or newer.

  • Added System Logs for Matter devices.

  • Added support for saving IGMP Querier addresses on non-querier switches.

  • Added Port Automations to automatically apply Port Profiles based on the connected device's vendor or MAC OUI.

  • Added a Wake-on-LAN option for wired clients.

    • Wake-on-LAN must be supported and enabled in the device's settings, such as its power settings or BIOS/UEFI. The device must remain connected to power, with its network adapter powered while asleep or shut down.

  • Improved Internet settings.

    • Added support for multiple VLANs on the same port.

    • Added a Passthrough VLANs setting.

  • Improved the Hotspot user experience.

    • Added a Personal Password for Each Guest option to generate unique passwords for guests to use across their devices.

    • Added an Isolate Guests option to assign each Personal WiFi guest to a separate network.

    • Added Guest Details to the Clients and Guests side panels.

    • Added an option to collect guest email addresses and export them via CSV or send them through Webhooks.

    • Added Webhook notifications when guest access ends.

    • Added CSV export and custom date selection.

    • Added support for custom fields, such as Student ID, in External Authorization.

    • Added support for Walled Garden links in Hotspot Landing Page settings.

    • Added an option to remove Powered by UniFi from the Hotspot Landing Page.

    • Improved External Authorization integration.

    • Improved guest data limit enforcement accuracy.

    • Improved guest authorization handling so revoking access for offline guests takes effect immediately on access points and gateways.

  • Improved the Orchestration Engine.

    • Added Device Template support.

    • Added Hotspot support.

    • Added Supernets support, allowing automatic subnet generation to prevent overlaps across sites.

    • Added Static Route support.

    • Added Port Profiles and Port Automations support.

  • Improved DHCP Guarding by synchronizing the configured IP address with the gateway IP for existing automatically created networks.

  • Improved Object creation by previewing automatically generated objects before saving.

  • Improved Channel AI.

  • Improved SD-WAN stability by preventing unnecessary tunnel reconnections on failover hubs when adding spokes.

  • Improved mesh adoption to prevent changes to Mesh Parent settings on other access points.

  • Improved statistics engine resiliency.

  • Improved application stability.

Bugfixes

  • Fixed an issue where the Site Manager Internet Health bar could temporarily show a site as offline after a Network Application update.

  • Fixed incorrect device time reporting for the Manitoba and Yukon time zones.

  • Fixed an issue where switch settings could not be edited after enabling Layer 3 routing.

  • Fixed an issue where devices connected to QSFP28 ports could display incorrect port numbers.

  • Fixed an issue where the Kill Switch could block internet access when a routed VPN client was paused.

  • Fixed an issue where Shadow Mode standby consoles could lose their Shadow Mode configuration if power was interrupted during a restore.

  • Fixed an issue where MC-LAG peer-link port configuration could drop keepalive traffic or tagged VLANs.

  • Fixed an issue where Port Lock did not work correctly with the main and backup ports of E7 access points.

  • Fixed an issue where blocking a client could fail when a nearby unadopted device was running older firmware.

  • Fixed an issue where blocked traffic from WireGuard clients was not displayed in Traffic Flows.

  • Fixed an issue where the UniFi Cellular Internet Backup option could be missing from Network settings.

  • Fixed a rare issue where Integration API requests could stall for up to 40 seconds.

  • Fixed an issue where UPS 2U Pro outlets could not be powered off remotely.

  • Fixed an issue where Site Manager could display incorrect Internet Health information.

  • Fixed an issue where some UniFi devices could show incorrect hostnames.

Additional information

 

Self-Hosted UniFi Deployments

For self-hosted deployments, we recommend transitioning to UniFi OS Server, which provides the full UniFi OS Platform experience, including the latest features, improvements, and integrations.

UniFi Cloud Gateways remain our recommended solution for deployments that do not require self-hosting.

title: CISA Adds Three Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
summary:
CISA has added three new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation.

  • CVE-2026-131914 Idunno AntiCsrf Deserialization of Untrusted Data Vulnerability 

  • CVE-2026-132165 Drupal Core Remote Code Execution Vulnerability 

  • CVE-2026-132224 Optimizely Web Experimentation External Control of Critical State Data Vulnerability 

These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise.

Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied.

While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities. CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria.

Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form. Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.

Vulnerabilities

CVE-2026-127280
C-More EA9 Programming Software V6.80 does not adequately validate data read from a project file before using it in heap memory operations. Remediations

Vendor fix

Mitigation
If you cannot update to the latest software or firmware version right away, apply the following compensating controls to reduce risk until the update can be performed. These measures are temporary and do not replace the update, which remains the primary and recommended remediation. Apply these controls as appropriate based on the vulnerability, assessed risk, operational requirements, and characteristics of your environment. Implement changes under your established management-of-change process. Before implementing isolation, access-control, or network-configuration changes, evaluate potential impacts to safety, availability, and essential operational functions. • Isolate affected engineering workstations and OT systems from external and nonessential networks, including the internet and corporate IT networks, where operationally feasible. • Disable or tightly restrict vendor, contractor, and other remote access to the affected OT environment until the vulnerability can be remediated. Where remote access is operationally required, use a hardened jump host, enforce multi-factor authentication, apply least-privilege access, and limit access to authorized, time-bound sessions. • Use trusted, dedicated OT networks for device communication. Where practicable and appropriate to the assessed risk, use dedicated or physically separated infrastructure for higher-criticality systems. Where logical segmentation is used, ensure segmentation controls are appropriately configured, secured, and monitored. • Restrict both physical and logical access to affected systems to authorized personnel only. Apply least-privilege principles to administrative, engineering, maintenance, and service access. • Configure application allowlisting, where supported, so that only trusted and pre-approved applications are permitted to execute. Block unauthorized software. • Use appropriate antivirus or endpoint detection and response (EDR) tools where supported and compatible with the affected system. Configure host-based and network firewalls to permit only required communications. • Disable unnecessary services, ports, protocols, and communication pathways associated with the affected systems. Where a service or protocol cannot be disabled for operational reasons, restrict access to trusted systems and authorized users wherever possible. • Enable and regularly review available system, security, and network logs to identify suspicious or unauthorized activity. Where appropriate, monitor communications to and from affected systems for unexpected connections or changes in network behavior. • Maintain secure, tested, and preferably offline backups of PLC programs, device configurations, engineering workstation configurations, and other information necessary to restore operations. Periodically verify that backups can be successfully restored. • Verify that critical OT functions can continue operating without unnecessary dependencies on external networks, cloud services, remote-access services, corporate IT services, or other nonessential systems. • If removable media is required to transfer files into an isolated or restricted environment, use controlled and trusted media and scan it for malicious content before use. • Continuously evaluate the risks associated with operating vulnerable or outdated firmware or software. Adjust compensating controls as the threat environment, operational requirements, or available vulnerability information changes. These compensating controls are intended to reduce exposure while remediation is pending. Organizations should prioritize applying the vendor-provided update as soon as it can be safely tested and deployed within the operational environment.

title: CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
summary:
CISA has added two new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation.

  • CVE-2026-133968 Project MONAI MONAI Label Path Traversal Vulnerability

  •  CVE-2026-134624 N-able Mail Assure (SpamExperts) Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) Vulnerability

These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise.

Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied.

While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities. CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria.

Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form. Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.

CISA has added four new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation. 

  • CVE-2024-10441 Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM) Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output Vulnerability
  • CVE-2026-40217 BerriAI LiteLLM Unprotected Alternate Channel Vulnerability
  • CVE-2026-90436 Apache Axis Unsafe Reflection Vulnerability
  • CVE-2026-90817 Vanderbilt University Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) Code Injection Vulnerability

These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise. 

Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. 

While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities. CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria. 

Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form. Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.

title: Attackers Used Optimizely to A/B Test Malware on Top Websites
summary: At least 178 top web destinations unwittingly served a variety of malware exploits against visitors over the past 24 hours thanks to a security vulnerability involving Optimizely, a company that helps websites customize user experiences and test out new features. Experts say the incident, which saw data-stealing malicious software silently injected into sites like the BBC, CNN, Equifax, Ledger and Zoom, was exacerbated by the reality that few popular websites enforce strict rules on the sources of third-party content.

title: UniFi Network Application 11.0.103
summary:
Overview

UniFi Network Application 11.0.103 requires UniFi OS 6.0 or newer and includes the improvements and bugfixes below.

If you are upgrading from 10.x or earlier versions, note that the PostgreSQL migration clears existing statistics history, and all sites are automatically migrated to Zone-Based Firewall. See 11.0.97 for details.

Improvements

  • Added support for matching networks in the External zone as Firewall Policy destinations.

Bugfixes

  • Fixed a rare issue where VPN Servers could fail to work.

  • Fixed a rare issue where UID Enterprise WiFi networks could fail to work.

  • Fixed an issue where Firewall Policies between networks could lose IPv6 port restrictions after upgrading from Network 10.6 with Legacy Firewall enabled.

  • Fixed an issue where Port Forwarding rules to networks routed by a Layer 3 switch did not work.

  • Fixed an issue where WAN OUT block rules could stop blocking VPN client traffic after upgrading from Network 10.6 with Legacy Firewall enabled.

  • Fixed a rare issue where the Devices page could fail to load.

  • Fixed an issue where Port Forwarding rules to hosts behind a static route could stop working after upgrading from Network 10.6 with Legacy Firewall enabled.

  • Fixed a rare issue where ULTE devices could unexpectedly display Verify Your Account.

  • Fixed a rare issue where upgrading to Network 11.0 could fail.

  • Fixed an issue where SD-WAN tunnels could temporarily disconnect after an upgrade.

  • Fixed a rare issue where the Default Network could be lost after an upgrade.

  • Fixed a rare issue where UID Enterprise WiFi broadcasting could fail.

Additional information

 

Self-Hosted UniFi Deployments

For self-hosted deployments, we recommend transitioning to UniFi OS Server, which provides the full UniFi OS Platform experience, including the latest features, improvements, and integrations.

UniFi Cloud Gateways remain our recommended solution for deployments that do not require self-hosting.

title: I joined the NTP Pool, but not with my Stratum 1 Pi
summary:
Before I get too deep into the time-nuts rabbit hole, I figured I should share a little bit of the good time I now have in my studio, with everyone else.

Thus, I've finally joined the NTP Pool, offering one public Stratum 2 NTP time server (ntp-01.jeffgeerling.com), which gets its time from my Stratum 1 time server (time.jeffgeerling.com) in the studio.

My Time Pi is connected to an outside GNSS antenna through a TimeHAT v6, which I paired with a high quality timing-grade GNSS module, the u-blox ZED-F9T.

  • Company Headquarters Location: United States

Vulnerabilities

CVE-2026-117659
The InfoScan Electron desktop client improperly handles TLS certificate errors by accepting certificates without validating their trustworthiness. The client also configures Electron with nodeIntegration enabled, contextIsolation disabled, and webSecurity disabled. These settings weaken the client’s security boundaries. An attacker who is able to intercept or manipulate network communications may be able to present an untrusted certificate without the application rejecting the connection.

This type of vulnerability is a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and poses significant risks to the federal enterprise.

Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied.

While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities. CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria.

Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form. Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.
